## energyRt ![energyRt hex logo](reference/figures/logo.png)

[![Lifecycle:
maturing](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-maturing-blue.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html)
[![License: Apache
2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0)

> **Energy-system planning, end to end in R.**

**energyRt** is an open-source, R-native framework and model generator
for least-cost energy-system planning. Describe resources, technologies,
storage, trade, and demand as reusable R objects; energyRt turns them
into a capacity-expansion and dispatch model, runs the solver, and
returns tidy results for analysis and reporting. Built-in validation
tools can then test model structure and solution identities.

The package supplies the modeling machinery rather than a fixed dataset
or scenario. It is intended for analysts, researchers, and educators who
want to build transparent models at the scale and resolution their
question requires without leaving the R ecosystem.

### Why energyRt

- **Model the system, not the algebra.** Work with energy-system
  components; energyRt generates sets, mappings, equations, solver
  files, and result tables.
- **Match resolution to the question.** Define the timeframes and
  timeslices your model needs in a nested
  [timescales](https://github.com/optimal2050/timescales) calendar, and
  balance different commodities at different levels of a regional
  hierarchy.
- **Keep one reproducible workflow.** Prepare data, compose scenarios,
  solve, validate, compare, plot, and report in R. Large scenarios can
  use Arrow-backed storage and lazy result loading.
- **Choose how and where to solve.** The same model can target
  GLPK/MathProg, Julia/JuMP, Python/Pyomo, or GAMS, with experimental
  direct-matrix and remote routes for larger problems.

### Time and space are yours to define

Resolution is a modelling choice, not a fixed property of the framework.
The calendar below nests `ANNUAL > SEASON > HOUR`; the geoscale nests
`nation > zone > region`. Both are declared by the modeller, and each
commodity balances at the level its data supports.

|  |  |
|----|----|
| ![A nested calendar: one annual slice over four seasons over 24 hours, sized by their share of the year](reference/figures/readme-calendar.png) | ![A three-level geoscale: regions nested in zones nested in one nation](reference/figures/readme-geoscale.png) |
| *`autoplot(calendars`$`s4_h24)</code> — 4 seasons x 24 hours, nested
under an annual balance.</em></td>
<td><em><code>plot_geoscale(topia`$`geoscales$continent)` — regions grouped into zones, coloured by zone.* |  |

**Changing a dimension does not mean rewriting the model.** A model is
declared once at full resolution; a coarser or sampled calendar is
passed at solve time, and the geography is attached, or filtered to a
sub-territory, the same way. Three arguments decide the resolution of a
run:

``` r

newModel(..., calendar = calendars$s4_h24)   # declared: 4 seasons x 24 hours
solve_model(mod, name = "sampled",           # solved on a subset of its slices
            calendar = calendars$s4_h24_subset_2seasons)
setGeoscale(mod, topia$geoscales$continent)  # nation > zone > region
```

In a small gas-and-demand model on that calendar, sampling two of the
four seasons cuts 101 timeslices to 51 and lands within 0.2% of the full
solve (1759.7 against 1756.8) — the usual reason to sample while
iterating and confirm at full resolution before reporting.

### What’s new in v0.90

Version 0.90 is the pre-release for v1.0 and the first release since
`v0.50-beta`, consolidating three unreleased development cycles. It
brings nested time and geography into the core model, re-models storage
as three priced parts, makes vintages and clusters one mechanism
(including graded resources that cannot pool), reworks interpolation and
scenario storage, adds structural validation and solution verification,
expands analysis and reporting
([`levcost()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/levcost.md),
[`report()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/report.md),
[`draw()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/draw.md), `autoplot()`), and
adopts the Apache-2.0 license.

What remains before v1.0 is testing, debugging and visualisation rather
than new structure. Upgrading from 0.50 is not a drop-in — see the
[release notes](https://energyrt.org/news/) and
[Upgrading](#upgrading-from-earlier-versions) first.

## Quickstart

This complete model has one fuel, one power plant, and one demand. On
Windows, GLPK is available with Rtools.

``` r

library(energyRt)

GAS <- newCommodity("GAS", timeframe = "ANNUAL")
ELC <- newCommodity("ELC", timeframe = "ANNUAL")

SUP_GAS <- newSupply("SUP_GAS", commodity = "GAS",
  supply = data.frame(cost = 6.0))                    # MEUR/PJ

EGAS <- newTechnology("EGAS",
  input   = list(comm = "GAS"),
  output  = list(comm = "ELC"),
  ceff    = data.frame(comm = "GAS", cinp2use = 0.55),
  invcost = list(invcost = 900),                     # MEUR/GW
  fixom   = 25,
  cap2act = 31.536,
  olife   = 25L)

DEM_ELC <- newDemand("DEM_ELC", commodity = "ELC",
  demand = data.frame(demand = 50))                  # PJ/year

mod <- newModel("HELLO",
  data = newRepository("parts", GAS, ELC, SUP_GAS, EGAS, DEM_ELC),
  region = "R1",
  discount = 0.05,
  horizon = newHorizon(
    period = 2025:2040,
    intervals = c(1, 5, 10),
    mid_is_end = TRUE
  ))

scen <- solve_model(mod, name = "BASE", solver = solver_options$glpk)

getData(scen, "vObjective", merge = TRUE)  # discounted system cost
getData(scen, "vTechCap", merge = TRUE)    # installed capacity
```

[`solve_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_model.md)
interpolates and solves in one call. To inspect or modify the
interpolated scenario, use the composable stages instead:

``` r

scen <- mod |>
  interpolate(name = "BASE") |>
  solve()
```

The [Get started](https://energyrt.org/articles/energyRt.html) vignette
explains the model and workflow step by step.

## Core capabilities

- **Reference energy systems** built from commodities, supply, demand,
  technologies, storage, weather, trade, taxes, subsidies, and custom
  constraints.
- **Capacity expansion and dispatch** across multiple planning periods,
  with investment, retirement, operating, resource, emissions, and
  policy constraints.
- **Nested time** using
  [timescales](https://github.com/optimal2050/timescales). The modeler
  defines the calendar hierarchy, timeslices, and their duration:
  energyRt imposes no fixed 8,760-slice ceiling. Full-resolution,
  representative, and sampled calendars can all mix different balancing
  timeframes in one model.
- **Nested geography** using
  [geoscales](https://github.com/optimal2050/geoscales), so national,
  zonal, and nodal balances can coexist and results can be mapped or
  aggregated.
- **One object, many processes.** A technology declares build
  **vintages** and parallel **clusters** — site grades, fleet types,
  tranches — and expands into ordinary processes, each with its own
  costs, efficiency and limits. Tiered commodities and tiered weather
  series give a graded resource its own balance and profile per grade,
  so the best sites run out before the next grade starts.
- **Storage as three parts.** Charger, reservoir and discharger are
  sized and priced separately, tied by duration and C-rate, with flows
  bounded by the converter rating.
- **Reusable scenarios** with recorded runs, a project registry, myopic,
  sampled, regional and guided solve workflows, and Arrow-backed
  persistence for results larger than memory.
- **Checks that catch silent nonsense.** Structural validation refuses a
  model that would solve to a meaningless answer — a flow with no
  capacity link, a constraint with no data behind it — and
  [`verify_solution()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/verify_solution.md)
  re-derives the model’s own identities from the results.
- **Analysis and communication** through tidy
  [`getData()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/getData.md) results,
  scenario and input comparison, levelized costs for technologies,
  storage and trade without a solver,
  [`draw()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/draw.md) diagrams,
  `autoplot()`, maps, and HTML/PDF/Word reports for any object.
- **A path from learning to application:** the packaged TOPIA teaching
  model develops a multi-region power system step by step, while
  [IDEEA](https://ideea-model.github.io/IDEEA/) demonstrates a
  production-scale application to India’s power system.

## A tour of the API

Each block below is the call shape, not a complete script — the
Quickstart above is the runnable one, and every topic has an article
behind it.

### Processes that extend rather than multiply

A technology converts any number of inputs into any number of outputs,
with auxiliary flows coupling its capacity or its flows to anything else
— land per MW, water or an emission per unit of fuel.
[`update()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/update.md) derives a variant
instead of re-typing the object.

``` r

EGAS <- newTechnology("EGAS",
  input   = data.frame(comm = "GAS", unit = "PJ"),
  output  = data.frame(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"),
  aux     = data.frame(acomm = "CO2", unit = "kt"),
  aeff    = data.frame(acomm = "CO2", comm = "GAS", cinp2aout = 56),
  af      = data.frame(af.up = 0.85),
  invcost = data.frame(invcost = 900),
  cap2act = 8.76)

EGAS_CCS <- update(EGAS, name = "EGAS_CCS",
  aeff = data.frame(acomm = "CO2", comm = "GAS", cinp2aout = 5.6))
```

### Supply, curves, trade and the model boundary

A flat price becomes a stepped supply curve in one call; corridors carry
a commodity between regions, with electrical wrappers and optional
loop-flow physics; imports and exports price what crosses the model
boundary.

``` r

SUP_GAS  <- newSupply("SUP_GAS", commodity = "GAS",
                      supply = data.frame(ava.up = 400))
SUP_GAS  <- asSupplyCurve(SUP_GAS, price = c(4, 6, 9))   # three priced steps

AC_R1_R2 <- newACLine("AC_R1_R2", commodity = "ELC",
                      from = "R1", to = "R2", reactance = 0.1)
IMP_ELC  <- newImport("IMP_ELC", commodity = "ELC",
                      import = data.frame(price = 5000))
```

### Variants: similar processes as one family

Build **vintages** and parallel **clusters** live on one object and
expand into ordinary processes, so a fleet or a graded resource is
declared once and analysed together — including its levelized cost,
member by member, without a solver.

``` r

EWIN <- newTechnology("EWIN",
  output  = data.frame(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"),
  cluster = data.frame(cluster = c("01", "02", "03"), order = 1:3),
  capacity = data.frame(cluster = c("01", "02", "03"), cap.up = c(8, 16, 40)),
  invcost  = data.frame(cluster = c("01", "02", "03"), invcost = c(600, 900, 1800)),
  vintage  = data.frame(olife = 25L), cap2act = 8.76)

getVariants(mod)                      # the names before interpolating
levcost(EWIN, by_variant = TRUE)      # USD/MWh per member
```

### Policy instruments and constraints

Taxes and subsidies levy on a commodity total or on named processes.
Beyond the ~150 equation families energyRt generates from your data,
[`newConstraint()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newConstraint.md)
writes an arbitrary linear restriction over declared summands — the two
below are TOPIA’s own carbon-price and no-new-nuclear levers.

``` r

CT_CO2 <- newTax(name = "CT_CO2", comm = "CO2",
  tax = data.frame(year = c(2030, 2050), bal = c(0.02, 0.08)))

NO_NEW_NUC <- newConstraint(name = "NO_NEW_NUC", eq = "<=",
  for.each = data.frame(year = years, tech = "ENUC"),
  term1 = list(variable = "vTechNewCap"),
  rhs = 0, defVal = 0)
```

### Solve strategies

The same model can be solved with perfect foresight or with any of four
alternatives, each recorded as a run of the scenario.

``` r

base   <- solve_model(mod, name = "base")                    # intertemporal
myopic <- solve_myopic(mod, name = "myopic", step = 1L)      # window by window
sampled <- solve_by_sample(mod, name = "sampled")            # sampled calendars
by_reg <- solve_by_region(mod, name = "by_region")           # region by region
guided <- solve_guided(mod, name = "guided")                 # toward a target
```

### Model size control

Resolution is the first lever — a coarser timeframe or geoframe for a
commodity, a sampled calendar, a subset of regions. Folding and sparse
storage are the second: they drop what does not vary and what equals a
default, losslessly.

``` r

scen <- interpolate_model(mod, fold = TRUE, sparse = TRUE)
model_size(scen)              # rows per parameter, largest first
scen <- trim_parameters(scen) # drop rows no mapping indexes
```

### Scenarios, tracking and queries

A project registry keyed on path records every model, scenario and
dataset, so a study with thousands of runs stays addressable by name.
Content hashes say whether two things are really the same, and results
are queried and compared without leaving R.

``` r

reg  <- load_registry()
scen <- getScenario("base")                     # by name, from the registry
scenario_runs(scen)                             # every solve of this scenario
model_hash(mod); object_hash(EGAS)              # content, not file names

getData(scen, name = "vTechCap", merge = TRUE, variants = TRUE)
compare_scenarios(list(base = base, carbon_tax = tax_run))
```

### Visualisation and auto-reporting

``` r

draw(EGAS)                                            # the process diagram
autoplot(scen, type = "generation", comm = "ELC", by = "cluster")
plot_map(scen, name = "vTechNewCap")                  # any variable with a region
report(scen, template = "full", format = "html")      # a full scenario datasheet
```

## One model, many representations and solve routes

The model definition is independent of the mathematical-programming
runtime. Choose a representation and solve route without rewriting the
energy-system model.

| Route | What it does | Good fit |
|----|----|----|
| [GLPK / MathProg](https://www.gnu.org/software/glpk/) | Writes MathProg and solves with GLPK | First models, teaching, and transparent local runs |
| [Julia / JuMP](https://jump.dev/) | Writes JuMP for HiGHS, CBC, GLPK, CPLEX, or cuOpt | Larger local models and a choice of algorithms |
| [Python / Pyomo](https://www.pyomo.org/) | Writes Pyomo for HiGHS, CBC, GLPK, or CPLEX | Python-based solver environments |
| [GAMS](https://www.gams.com/) | Writes GAMS for solvers such as CPLEX or CBC | Existing institutional GAMS workflows |
| [multimod](https://github.com/optimal2050/multimod) *(experimental)* | Converts through a common AST to LaTeX, backend code, or an LP/MPS matrix | Translation, mathematical documentation, inspection, and direct LP assembly |

**multimod is more than another solver backend.** It parses energyRt’s
model into a language-neutral abstract syntax tree, from which it can
render the mathematical formulation in LaTeX, emit code for other
modeling languages, or skip generated model code and assemble the LP
matrix directly. The direct route writes MPS and avoids the symbolic
model-build step that can dominate time and memory on large linear
problems.

The same separation extends to remote execution.
[NEOS](https://neos-server.org/) can run supported solver jobs remotely.
The experimental [mmcloud](https://github.com/optimal2050/mmcloud) route
sends model files to cloud hardware, runs the solver there, streams its
progress, and retrieves the solution. Together, multimod and mmcloud let
energyRt assemble a large LP locally and solve it on cloud GPUs when it
exceeds the practical capacity of a workstation.

See [Solver backends](https://energyrt.org/articles/backends.html) for
setup, presets, limitations, and validation guidance.

## Installation

Install the development release from GitHub:

``` r

pak::pkg_install("optimal2050/energyRt")
```

`pak` installs energyRt’s R dependencies, including the optimal2050
packages listed in `DESCRIPTION`. You also need at least one solver
runtime. On Windows, Rtools includes GLPK; on other platforms, install
GLPK separately or configure Julia/JuMP, Python/Pyomo, or GAMS.

After installation, check the local setup:

``` r

library(energyRt)
en_setup()
en_check_dependencies()
```

See the [installation guide](https://energyrt.org/articles/install.html)
for platform-specific instructions.

  resolution](https://energyrt.org/articles/space-resolution.html) —
  user-defined nested calendars and regional hierarchies.
- [Storage](https://energyrt.org/articles/storage.html) and [Vintages &
  clusters](https://energyrt.org/articles/variants.html) — the two
  classes with the most structure, worked through end to end.
- [Units](https://energyrt.org/articles/units.html) — stating units, and
  the capacity-to-activity conversion.
- [TOPIA I](https://energyrt.org/articles/topia-build.html),
  [II](https://energyrt.org/articles/topia-use.html) and
  [III](https://energyrt.org/articles/region-aggregation.html) — build a
  complete teaching model, run scenarios on it, then aggregate its
  regions.

  management](https://energyrt.org/articles/scenario-management.html),
  and [reports](https://energyrt.org/articles/reports.html) — move from
  a model to a reproducible study.
- [Roadmap](https://energyrt.org/articles/roadmap.html) — current status
  and priorities on the way to v1.0.

## Upgrading from earlier versions

v0.90 removes deprecated names and compatibility shims from the 0.8
series and changes several serialized model and scenario structures.
Rebuild saved inputs from their source definitions and review the
[release notes](https://energyrt.org/news/) before comparing results.

To reproduce a pre-2026 project without migrating it, install the frozen
legacy release:

``` r

pak::pkg_install("optimal2050/energyRt@v0.50-beta")
```

energyRt v0.90 is under active development. Please report bugs and
proposed improvements in the [issue
tracker](https://github.com/optimal2050/energyRt/issues). The package
website is <https://energyrt.org>.

# Package index

## Model components

The S4 classes a model is made of. Each is built by its `new*()`
constructor below and carries its data in slots.

- [`class-calendar`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-calendar.md) :
  An S4 class to represent sub-annual time resolution structure.
- [`class-commodity`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-commodity.md)
  : An S4 class to represent a commodity
- [`class-config`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-config.md) : An
  S4 class to represent default model configuration.
- [`class-constraint`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-constraint.md)
  [`class-summand`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-constraint.md)
  [`summand-class`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-constraint.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : An S4 class to represent a custom constraint.
- [`class-costs`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-costs.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : An S4 class to add costs to objective function
- [`class-demand`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-demand.md) : An
  S4 class to declare a demand in the model
- [`class-export`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-export.md) : An
  S4 class to represent commodity export to the rest of the world.
- [`class-horizon`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-horizon.md) :
  An S4 class to represent model/scenario planning horizon with
  intervals (year-steps)
- [`class-import`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-import.md) : An
  S4 class to represent commodity import from the rest of the world.
- [`class-model`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-model.md)
  [`model`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-model.md) : An S4 class
  to represent model
- [`class-modInp`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-modInp.md) : An
  S4 class to represent model input
- [`class-modOut`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-modOut.md) : An
  S4 class to store results of a solved scenario
- [`class-parameter`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-parameter.md)
  : An S4 class to specify the model set or parameter
- [`class-repository`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-repository.md)
  : An S4 class to store the model objects.
- [`class-scenario`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-scenario.md)
  [`scenario`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-scenario.md) : An S4
  class to represent scenario, an interpolated and/or solved model.
- [`class-settings`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-settings.md) :
  An S4 class to represent scenario settings
- [`class-technology`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-technology.md)
  : An S4 class to represent technology
- [`class-trade`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-trade.md) : An S4
  class to represent inter-regional trade
- [`class-variable`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-variable.md) :
  An S4 class to specify a model variable
- [`class-weather`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-weather.md) :
  S4 class to represent weather factors
- [`storage-class`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-storage.md) :
  An S4 class to represent storage type of technological process.
- [`subsidy-class`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-subsidy.md) :
  An S4 class to represent a commodity subsidy
- [`tax-class`](https://energyRt.org/reference/class-tax.md) : An S4
  class to represent a commodity tax
- [`supply-class`](https://energyRt.org/reference/supply-class.md) : An
  S4 class to represent a supply of a commodity

## Building a model

Constructors for the objects above, the repository that holds them, and
the model that binds them to a calendar, regions and a horizon.

- [`newModel()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newModel.md)
  [`setHorizon(`*`<model>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newModel.md)
  [`getHorizon(`*`<model>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newModel.md)
  : Create new model object
- [`newRepository()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newRepository.md) :
  A constructor for the repository class
- [`newCommodity()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newCommodity.md) :
  Create new commodity object
- [`newTechnology()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/technology.md)
  [`update(`*`<technology>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/technology.md)
  : Create a new "technology" object.
- [`newStorage()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/storage.md) : Create
  new storage object
- [`newSupply()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newSupply.md) :
  Constructor for supply object.
- [`newDemand()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newDemand.md)
  [`update(`*`<demand>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newDemand.md)
  : Create new demand object
- [`newTrade()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newTrade.md) : Create
  new trade object
- [`newACLine()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newACLine.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Create an AC transmission line
- [`newDCLink()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newDCLink.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Create a DC transmission link
- [`newImport()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newImport.md) : Create
  new export object
- [`newExport()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newExport.md)
  [`update(`*`<export>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newExport.md)
  : Create new export object
- [`newWeather()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newWeather.md)
  [`update(`*`<weather>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newWeather.md)
  : Create new weather object
- [`newConstraint()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newConstraint.md) :
  Create constraint object to add custom constraints to the model.
- [`newCosts()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newCosts.md) : Create
  new costs object
- [`newTax()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newTax.md) : Create a new
  tax object
- [`newSubsidy()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newSubsidy.md) :
  Create a new subsidy object
- [`newScenario()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newScenario.md) :
  Generate a new scenario object
- [`newRegistry()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/registry.md)
  [`load_registry()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/registry.md)
  [`save_registry()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/registry.md)
  [`add_to_registry()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/registry.md)
  [`add(`*`<en_registry>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/registry.md)
  [`summary(`*`<en_registry>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/registry.md)
  [`find_in_registry()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/registry.md)
  [`refresh_registry()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/registry.md) :
  Project registry of models, scenarios, and runs
- [`add(`*`<repository>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/add.md)
  [`add(`*`<model>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/add.md) : Add an
  object to the model's repository
- [`update(`*`<supply>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/update.md)
  [`update(`*`<storage>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/update.md)
  [`update(`*`<trade>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/update.md)
  [`update(`*`<import>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/update.md) :
  Update supply object
- [`asSupplyCurve()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/supply-curve.md)
  [`asImportCurve()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/supply-curve.md)
  [`asExportCurve()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/supply-curve.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Stepped supply, export and import curves
- [`lossTranches()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/lossTranches.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Loss tranches for a transmission line
- [`combine_vintages()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/combine_vintages.md)
  : Combine per-vintage technology objects into one vintaged technology

## Time resolution

Calendars and horizons. The shipped `calendars` catalog is generated
with the sibling *timescales* package;
[`newCalendar()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newCalendar.md) builds
your own.

- [`newCalendar()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newCalendar.md) :
  Generate a new calendar object from
- [`newHorizon()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newHorizon.md)
  [`update(`*`<horizon>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newHorizon.md)
  [`setHorizon(`*`<config>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newHorizon.md)
  [`update(`*`<config>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/newHorizon.md)
  : Create a new object of class 'horizon'
- [`calendars`](https://energyRt.org/reference/calendars.md) : Example
  calendars
- [`horizons`](https://energyRt.org/reference/horizons.md) : Example
  planning horizons
- [`tsl_sets`](https://energyRt.org/reference/timeslices.md)
  [`tsl_levels`](https://energyRt.org/reference/timeslices.md) : Sets of
  the common formats with structure
- [`make_timetable()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/calendar.md) :
  Create timetable of time-timeslices from given structure as a list
- [`autoplot(`*`<calendar>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/plot_calendar_method.md)
  : Visualize a Calendar object
- [`autoplot(`*`<horizon>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/plot_horizon_method.md)
  : Visualize a Horizon object
- [`year_label()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/year_label.md) :
  Display labels of the model's milestone years

## Space resolution

Multi-level regions. A commodity declares the level it balances on, and
coarse balances roll up without a `trade` route for every pair.

- [`setCalendar(`*`<config>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`setGeoscale(`*`<config>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`getGeoscale(`*`<config>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`setGeoscale(`*`<model>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`getGeoscale(`*`<model>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`setGeoscale(`*`<scenario>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`getGeoscale(`*`<scenario>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`getCalendar(`*`<config>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`getCalendar(`*`<model>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  [`getCalendar(`*`<scenario>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/setGeoscale.md)
  : Attach or read a model's geoscale

- [`get_process_groups()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_groups.md)
  : Technologies that may be merged into one clustered object

- [`process_cluster_sweep()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/process_cluster_sweep.md)
  :

  Sweep a technology family's clusterings, to choose `k` by looking

- [`model_clusters()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/model_clusters.md)
  : The clustering behind an aggregated model

- [`check_geoscale_regions()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/check_geoscale_regions.md)
  : Check a geoscale against the model's declared regions

- [`plot_geoscale()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/plot_geoscale.md) :
  Draw a model's geoscale

- [`get_region()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_region.md) :
  Collect the regions an object operates in

- [`subset_model_regions()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/subset_model_regions.md)
  : Restrict a model to a region subset

- [`aggregate_model_regions()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/aggregate_model_regions.md)
  : Aggregate a model to a coarser set of regions

## Process specifications

Portable YAML/JSON process definitions, and the interactive designer.

- [`process_from_spec()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/process_from_spec.md)
  : Build a process object from a spec

- [`process_to_spec()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/process_to_spec.md)
  : Export a process object as a spec list

- [`process_spec_code()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/process_spec_code.md)
  : The constructor call equivalent to a process spec, as text

- [`process_spec_issues()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/process_spec_issues.md)
  : Validate a process spec and report issues

- [`read_process_spec()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/read_process_spec.md)
  : Read and validate a process spec

- [`process_designer()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/process_designer.md)
  : Launch the process designer

- [`read_technology_xlsx()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/read_technology_xlsx.md)
  :

  Read `technology` object(s) from an Excel workbook

- [`write_technology_xlsx()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/write_technology_xlsx.md)
  :

  Write `technology` object(s) to an Excel workbook

## Interpolating and solving

The core pipeline.
[`solve_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_model.md) does
the whole sequence; the separate verbs let a stage be inspected or
re-run.

- [`interpolate_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/interpolate_model.md)
  [`interpolate(`*`<model>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/interpolate_model.md)
  : Interpolate a model into a solver-ready scenario
- [`solve_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_model.md)
  [`solve_scenario()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_model.md)
  [`solve(`*`<model>`*`,`*`<character>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_model.md)
  : Solve a model or an interpolated scenario
- [`write_script()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/write.md)
  [`write_sc()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/write.md) : Write
  scenario object as a Python, Julia, GAMS, or MathProg script with data
  files to a directory
- [`read_solution()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/read.md)
  [`read(`*`<scenario>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/read.md) :
  Read a solved run's solution into a scenario
- [`read_sequence()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/read_sequence.md) :
  Rebuild a solve sequence from the variants on disk
- [`with_solver_log()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/with_solver_log.md)
  : Send the solver's progress log to a file

## multimod

Converting an interpolated scenario into a
[multimod](https://github.com/optimal2050/multimod) model, which can
then be rendered to any backend multimod supports or assembled straight
into a matrix and solved. multimod is a suggested package; these are
no-ops without it.

- [`as_multimod(`*`<scenario>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/as_multimod.scenario.md)
  : Build a multimod model from an interpolated scenario
- [`multimod_import_data()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/multimod_import_data.md)
  : Import energyRt scenario data into a multimod model
- [`multimod_import_log()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/multimod_import_log.md)
  : Get data import log from model
- [`multimod_unmatched()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/multimod_unmatched.md)
  : Show unmatched elements
- [`multimod_from_energyRt()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/multimod_from_energyRt.md)
  : Build a multimod model from an interpolated energyRt scenario

## Remote and cloud solving

Solving where you are not: the NEOS server for GAMS/CPLEX without a
local licence, and GPU/cloud execution for models too large for a
laptop.

  [`neos_list_solvers()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/neos.md) : NEOS
  Server client (query the remote solver service)
- [`get_neos_email()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/neos_email.md)
  [`set_neos_email()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/neos_email.md) :
  NEOS submission email

  [`set_hf_token()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/hf_token.md) :
  Hugging Face access token

## Solve drivers

Sequences of solves — myopic foresight, sampled calendars,
region-by-region decomposition, and guided target-seeking — with their
primitives.

- [`solve_myopic()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_myopic.md) :
  Solve a model sequentially (myopic foresight)
- [`solve_by_sample()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_by_sample.md)
  : Solve a model on samples of its calendar
- [`solve_by_region()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_by_region.md)
  : Solve a model region by region
- [`solve_guided()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solve_guided.md) :
  Solve a model with guided perfect foresight
- [`horizon_windows()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/horizon_windows.md)
  : Split a horizon into sequential solve windows
- [`solution_ledger()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solution_ledger.md)
  : Extract the carry-forward ledger from a solved scenario
- [`apply_ledger()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/apply_ledger.md) :
  Apply a carry ledger to a model
- [`myopic_objective()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/myopic_objective.md)
  : Globally discounted total cost of a myopic sequence
- [`calendar_samples()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/calendar_samples.md)
  : Build a calendar-sample specification
- [`sample_summary()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/sample_summary.md)
  : Summarise an ensemble across samples
- [`boundary_window()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/boundary_window.md)
  : A generic boundary trade window
- [`guided_windows()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/guided_windows.md)
  : Two-milestone windows for a guided solve
- [`guided_gap()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/guided_gap.md) : Cost
  of the guidance
- [`solution_targets()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/solution_targets.md)
  : Capacity targets from a solved scenario
- [`apply_targets()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/apply_targets.md) :
  Impose capacity targets on a model

  Retrieve model objects from a repository, model or scenario

- [`findData()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/findData.md) :

- [`find_in_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/find_in_model.md) :

- [`findDuplicates()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/findDuplicates.md)

- [`size()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/size.md) : Size of an object

  : Split a storage level into duration bands

## Saving and loading

Models, repositories and scenarios on disk — Arrow-backed, so results
larger than memory stay readable.

- [`save_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/model_store.md)
  [`load_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/model_store.md) : Save
  a model to / load a model from the model store

- [`save_repository()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/repo_store.md)
  [`load_repository()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/repo_store.md) :
  Save a repository to / load a repository from the repository store

- [`save_scenario()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/save_scenario.md) :

  Save scenario object on disk in parquet format using `arrow` package.

- [`load_scenario()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/load_scenario.md)
  [`load_scenarios()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/load_scenario.md)
  : Load scenario (in progress)

- [`seal_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`unseal_model()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`seal_repository()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`unseal_repository()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`seal_dataset()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`unseal_dataset()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`seal_scenario()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`unseal_scenario()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`mark_delete()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`unmark_delete()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md)
  [`delete_marked()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/seal.md) : Seal and
  unseal store entries; mark them for deletion

- [`model_hash()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/model_hash.md)
  [`object_hash()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/model_hash.md) :
  Content hash of a model

- [`repository_hash()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/repository_hash.md)
  : Content hash of a repository

- [`dataset_hash()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/dataset_store.md)
  [`save_dataset()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/dataset_store.md)
  [`load_dataset()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/dataset_store.md) :
  Content hash of a dataset payload

- [`isInMemory()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/isInMemory.md) : Is
  object stored in memory?

- [`isOnDisk()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/isOnDisk.md) : Is object
  stored on disk?

- [`obj2mem()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/obj2mem.md) : Loads
  objects from disk to memory

- [`materialize_weather()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/materialize_weather.md)

## Validation and diagnostics

Checks on a model’s inputs, on an interpolated scenario, and on a solved
one.
[`verify_solution()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/verify_solution.md)
re-derives the model’s identities from the results.

- [`validate_scenario_parameters()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/validate_scenario_parameters.md)
  : Validate interpolated scenario parameters

- [`verify_solution()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/verify_solution.md)
  : Verify accounting identities of a solved scenario

- [`verify_checks()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/verify_checks.md) :

  Checks available to
  [`verify_solution()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/verify_solution.md)

- [`process_operability()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/process_operability.md)
  : Declared processes that cannot operate

- [`audit_coefficients()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/audit_coefficients.md)
  : Coefficient-range audit of a written model

- [`en_check_glpk()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  [`en_check_julia()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  [`en_check_python()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  [`en_check_pyomo()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  [`en_check_gams()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  [`en_check_gdx()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  [`en_check_julia_pkgs()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  [`en_check_solve()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  [`en_check_dependencies()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check.md)
  : Detect external solver software and dependencies

- [`en_check_packages()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/en_check_packages.md)
  : Check R package and external-tool dependencies

- [`trim_parameters()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/trim_parameters.md)
  : Trim numeric/bounds parameters to the domain of the maps that index
  them

- [`update_parameter()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/update_parameter.md)
  : Update parameter in the scenario by adding data to it

  Synthetic input shapes on a calendar (deterministic)

  : TOPIA input profiles (deterministic)

  : Catalogue of the model vocabulary

  prefix multipliers

  Solver presets
- [`vre_cf`](https://energyRt.org/reference/vre_cf.md) : Hourly wind and
  solar capacity factors, one site, one year
- [`vre_storage_duration`](https://energyRt.org/reference/vre_storage_duration.md)
  : Duration bands of a full-year battery, precomputed

## Utilities

Small helpers, conversions and accessors.

  : Get auxiliary commodities for each process

  : Get class of processes

- [`get_process_comm()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_comm.md)
  : Commodities associated with a processes

- [`get_process_groups()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_groups.md)
  : Technologies that may be merged into one clustered object

- [`get_process_inputs()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_inputs.md)
  : Get inputs of processes

- [`get_process_invest_window()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_invest_window.md)
  : Start and end years for process by region

- [`get_process_outputs()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_outputs.md)
  : Get output commodities for each process

- [`get_process_region()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_region.md)
  : Get regions for each process

- [`get_process_stored()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_stored.md)
  : Stored commodities of each process

- [`get_process_timeframe()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/get_process_timeframe.md)
  : Get operational timeframe of processes

- [`getUnits(`*`<commodity>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/getUnits.md)
  [`getUnits(`*`<technology>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/getUnits.md)
  [`getUnits(`*`<supply>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/getUnits.md)
  [`getUnits(`*`<demand>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/getUnits.md)
  [`getUnits(`*`<import>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/getUnits.md)
  [`getUnits(`*`<export>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/getUnits.md)
  [`getUnits(`*`<storage>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/getUnits.md)
  : Get parameter units for energyRt class objects

- [`commodity_properties()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/commodity_properties.md)
  : Recognised commodity properties

- [`commodity_property()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/commodity_property.md)
  : Physical property of a commodity

- [`convert_data`](https://energyRt.org/reference/convert_data.md) :

  Basic units conversion database for `convert` methods

- [`convert(`*`<character>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/convert.md)
  [`convert(`*`<numeric>`*`)`](https://energyRt.org/reference/convert.md)

  : Convert units

- [`renameSets()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/renameSets.md) :
  Rename data.frame columns of list of data.frames.

- [`revalueSets()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/revalueSets.md) :
  Replace specified values with new values in factor or character
  columns of a data.frame.

- [`register_weather_transform()`](https://energyRt.org/reference/register_weather_transform.md)
  : Register a weather transform for the session
